member_targets: The means or criteria by which an AI service itself tells apart information carried over as retained internal state versus information supplied at runtime through external reconstruction (summaries, retrieved records, user-provided history).
Whether, and by what observable response-level signatures or tests, retained internal state can be told apart from externally supplied context using only the AI's outward outputs.

The practical/operational differences between supplying prior information externally at runtime (summaries, retrieved records, user-provided history) versus carrying forward retained internal state, given that both can produce similar continuity behavior.
Methods or diagnostic procedures by which an observer could distinguish internally persisted context from externally supplied/reconstructed context in an AI system.

Whether and how retained internal state versus externally supplied context can be told apart from response behavior alone — i.e., the existence and nature of an observable discriminating criterion available to an outside observer.

A comparative evaluation of fidelity — how accurate and relevant externally supplied continuity (summaries, retrieved records, user-provided history) is relative to information held in retained full internal state across generations.

The mechanism or procedure by which a system selects and weights which parts of supplied summaries/retrieved records count as relevant for a new generation.

The set of practical investigative or testing methods (e.g., architectural inspection, controlled input manipulation, instrumentation of retrieval channels) capable of reliably determining whether observed continuity arises from internal persistence versus externally supplied context.
